categories.finding: National achievement → AI challenge → community → event formats → invitation → title.

Founders and developers are visible by 17–18s, with students in the draft. The event format becomes clear at 27–29s.
Caption states, stacked video rectangles and image collages carry the sequence; fast footage changes are visible but exact transition paths are unresolved.
The dark AI question gives way to bright community scenes; the film later uses sports and launches as associative bridges to the invitation.
Monochrome news, warm gatherings, white collage fields and a dark title mix documentary-looking and promotional imagery.
Tall serif text names the argument and event types, but some phrases span several brief shots. Practical attendance details are missing.

categories.finding: Visual captions preserve the national challenge, audience and event formats; no silent route to registration is given.
Large serif labels direct attention, but people and busy footage sometimes compete with the changing words.
The 47s film introduces history, AI, community and four formats; the final montage takes space that could hold attendance information.
The question about keeping up is answered by collective building and named events, though no completed participant project is shown.
National pride and uncertainty turn into belonging and confidence; this is interpreted intent, not a measured response.
India and building recur across otherwise varied footage; there is no single participant journey.
Biggest-movement, every-major-city and leadership claims are promotional statements. Attendance, coverage and learning outcomes are not verified.
Indian technology, payments, cricket and local gatherings give the event a specific cultural context.
Use part of the closing montage for concrete attendance information.
